item.title: [ 37] Charlie Cucked: MIGA fucks up everything, even creating a martyr
item.description:
Charlie Kirk has been transformed into an internet laughing stock, with his legacy destroyed by grifters and his wife.

https://theintercept.com/2026/09/07/charlie-kirk-internet-meme/

In the year since he was gunned down at an event at Utah Valley University, the Turning Point USA founder has gone from a man cut down in his prime to a recurring internet meme, complete with an AI-generated song, “We Are Charlie Kirk,” which hit No. 1 on Spotify’s Viral 50 U.S. ranking. Audio of his killing became a TikTok sound for girlie outfit transformation videos; he’s been inserted into movies like “Avatar” and “The Odyssey”; he’s been AI’d into Studio Ghibli-style art, the final scene of “The Sopranos,” and the video game “Grand Theft Auto.” Even the moment of his death has gotten the meme treatment, with parodies depicting him with Jeffrey Epstein and Benjamin Netanyahu.

The ridicule comes as a product of the American right’s insistence that Kirk’s violent death be taken seriously. They fought back hard against the meme-making and serious critique alike, weaponizing the conservative college-whisperer’s death to broadly crack down on free speech.

President Trump and his allies almost immediately blamed Democrats and “the radical left,” without evidence, for Kirk’s assassination. At the Department of Defense, Secretary Pete Hegseth promised to investigate whether members of the armed forces were inadequately mournful and terminate them. The State Department revoked visas of noncitizens who “celebrated” Kirk’s death. Local cops got in on the civil rights-bashing fun, too: A Tennessee man was arrested for posting a meme in the wake of Kirk’s death, amid a wave of firings in the state on similarly unstable grounds.

item.title: [194] /pcg/ - Pokémon Champions General
item.description:
Mega Salamence edition

Pokémon Champions is a free to play online battle simulator available on Switch and mobile. It features ranked, casual and private battles for both singles and doubles, and will be used for VGC tournaments in 2026.

>News
Reg MC is now live.

>Resources and useful links
Community Tournaments usage data: https://pikalytics.com/
Ladder usage data: https://pokechamdb.com/en

New Player Guide(NEW PEOPLE READ THIS):
https://rentry.org/pcg-guide (now taking suggestions and feedback)
Anon made guide for brand new players to make a viable team with the starting pokemon: https://teamsheet.gg/t/sample-beginner-reg-b-vl3698

Quick FAQ
>Do I need my own Pokémon to play?
No, the game features a recruitment system, but transferring from Home is recommended to save time and resources.
>What makes the game so much more accessible than before?
All aspects of a Pokémon are customizable with VP, a currency earned simply by playing the game. IVs are also removed.
Ask in the thread if you want any specific Pokémon, and someone will respond.
>Is there single player content?
No.
>Do I need a Nintendo Online subscription?
No.
>What's the starter pack?
US$6.99 one time purchase for 50 training tickets (fully train for free), 30 Teammate Tickets (recruit Pokemon without using VP), 50 extra box space and the LGPE trainer music. Only available on Switch for now.
>Is anything locked behind a paywall?
So far everything gameplay relevant is also purchasable with VP. Only E-Floette require ZA transfer.

item.title: [ 66] JAPAN IS DOOMED
item.description:
Japan has lost all of it's high tech industries. 30 years ago, it was completing head2head with America in every single technological field, today it's probably the least advanced G7 nation and is still falling behind. People shit on the A.I bubble or China's overcapacity in high end manufacturing, but at the end of the day, at least they have the tech, even if they had to spend an insane amount of money and debt to achieve it. The dotcom bubble didn't end the internet after all and America continued to dominate the internet age afterwards.

Meanwhile, Japan both has a massive debt crisis and is still falling behind badly. item.title: [ 31] Unova's design philosophy should've been explored more
item.description:
Long OP but I don't think people give enough credit to how Gamefreak designed the Unova region.
This was the first region outside of Japan and because they could no longer rely on their deep understanding of whatever Japanese region they were making, they opted to only loosely base Unova on New York and then added a bunch of their own ideas.

The New York influence is obvious in places like Castelia, Nimbasa, and the bridges, but they never let the inspiration chain the game down. Mixed in with the New York stuff was a bunch of weird fantasy locations that I'd expect to see in Dragon Quest and not Pokemon: Chargestone Cave, Relic Castle, Dragonspiral Tower, etc. and it made for a really unique region.

You can obviously criticize this approach by saying it makes Unova feel too "videogamey" like it's not a real place you can envision existing, and compared to places like Johto or Sinnoh thats true, but those older regions only had that level of depth because Gamefreak literally live in the country it's based on. Moving on to newer regions without that understanding, they all just feel like caricatures of the real world. "Poke-Paris" "Poke-London" or "Poke-Barcelona" don't do much to capture my attention, and when that kind of inspiration is all a region has, it makes everything feel flatter and less real.

tldr: I like how Unova only loosely used New York as a base and mixed in a lot of original ideas that no other region has quite done, with the exception maybe being Paldea's Area Zero.

https://www.the-independent.com/news/world/americas/911-air-quality-report-mamdani-ground-zero-b3046630.html

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani released more than 170,000 pages of internal records Tuesday that show officials misled people about the safety of the air around Ground Zero after the September 11 terror attacks.

“People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air,” Mamdani said during a news conference.

The move came just days before the U.S. is set to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the al Qaeda hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people when passenger planes toppled the World Trade Center’s Twin Towers, damaged the Pentagon and crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania.

Comedian and activist Jon Stewart, an outspoken supporter of first responders who were sickened while searching for remains at Ground Zero, also spoke at Mamdani’s City Hall news conference.

“There was poison in the air, and on the ground, and in the window sills, and in your air conditioners, and covering your pets and your clothes, and it stayed there for months,” he said. “Everyone knew. Now it’s very clear that the city knew as well.”

Key findings from the documents, which were reviewed by The New York Times before Tuesday’s announcement, include:

• Asbestos levels in dust samples throughout lower Manhattan exceeded hazardous limits in the days after September 11.

• Asbestos and other contaminants were found above acceptable limits in dust and air in lower Manhattan.

• A November 2011 audit showed levels of the carcinogen benzene were still spiking in the air around the towers’ footprints.

• That audit also showed that the amount of asbestos in the air at the Fresh Kills landfill on Staten Island increased after the attacks.

item.title: [ 84] Fuel prices at record Labor Day high in US thanks to trump's failing Iran War
item.description:
https://apnews.com/article/labor-day-record-high-gas-prices-dffb7d3fa06ef930aaeebc380e5e4e0e

It’s never been more expensive in the U.S. to fill up the tank and take one last summer trip over the Labor Day weekend.

The average price of regular gas was $4.14 a gallon heading into the holiday, nearly a dollar higher than last year and well above the Labor Day weekend record of $3.82 from 2012, according to AAA motor club.

Nicole Collins planned to head from Philadelphia to South Carolina to visit friends, but she said her family has spent most of the summer close to home and not taking their typical weekend trips because driving has gotten so expensive.

“Gas is pretty high right now. It doesn’t help that we also have a baby, so we also have to pay for that,” Collins said outside a gas station in Claymont, Delaware, where regular gas was $4.199 a gallon.

Prices shot up after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in February and have not settled down since. Crude oil traffic through the key Strait of Hormuz has plunged, and Iran has refused to reopen the waterway.

“Everything points to the Iran War and the Strait of Hormuz,” said Tom Seng, a professor of energy finance at Texas Christian University.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright offered few specifics on when the nation’s drivers might see relief at the gas pump, acknowledging that prices are higher now than Labor Day 2025.

But diesel is a different story: It hit a national average of $5.85 a gallon Friday, a record.

Trucks and other freight delivery systems use a lot of diesel, and that increased transportation cost is being passed on to consumers, whether at the grocery store or through package delivery services.

“It doesn’t really seem like there’s an end to it,” Collins said.

Former Pentagon AI Policy Director Mark Beall warned that expanding artificial intelligence surveillance tools, like Flock cameras, could turn American communities into a “China-like surveillance state” unless guardrails are enforced.

Speaking on “Saturday in America,” Beall argued that while this technology can have vital law enforcement benefits, clear rules and judicial oversight are necessary to protect the rights of Americans at home.

“We have to be careful that we don’t go too far to the other direction and create a China-like surveillance state, which is literally what AI capabilities will ultimately enable and are enabling right now,” Beall told Fox News.

From destroyed camera poles to viral signs blocking surveillance lenses, some communities are pushing back against neighborhood surveillance cameras. Flock cameras are automated license plate readers used by law enforcement to record vehicle data that can aid criminal investigations. People in communities with the cameras have raised concerns about privacy and potential misuse by law enforcement.

Beall acknowledged that the technology can benefit law enforcement but said people’s privacy concerns are also valid. He urged a compromise and called for guardrails on how the cameras can be used, including strict rules and court oversight to prevent officers from abusing the technology for personal reasons.

“It’s tough to bring the message of compromise to the American people, especially when it comes to our constitutional protections,” Beall said.

Only thing i could think would be a challenge is winter, but even then i think a 4x4 and backup heating/electricity and lots of firewood. It would also give good homesteading opportunities.

Anyways, is there any truth to the danger or is it just the average small-town tall tales and superstitions? Seems unlikely to me as I feel like if it was so dangerous you'd be seeing a lot more of it in the news.

item.title: [225] Freediving / Spearfishing
item.description:
General thread for freediving and/or spearfishing, since I don't see one mentioning either.

My personal questions:
I've been thinking about taking a certification course so I can learn to do these things correctly and safely. I'm probably happy just doing the diving, but spearfishing seems like an easy and practical extension. I only casually skindive and rod-and-reel fish at the moment. Does anyone have experience taking such a course?
I know I'll need my own gear early on, but each instructor I can find seems to have their own equipment shops, so I imagine they wouldn't be impartial about the quality of other gear on the market. I live on the Pacific coast of the US, so I see that a 7 mm open cell wetsuit is strongly recommended. What good/bad features should I look out for on wetsuits and other equipment? For non-competitive diving, carbon fiber fins are almost certainly not worth the price, right?
